1.title: Set the Table!
1.topic: a boy helps set the table for a family dinner before Aunt Kim arrives: a mat, a cup, a fork and a dish for each person, the cat hops up on the table and has to get down, and Aunt Kim hugs him for his big help (family, holidays, helping)
sounds: 짧게 '애': mat '맷', cat '캣'. '매트'처럼 끝에 '으'를 붙이지 않아요.
입을 살짝 벌리고 짧게 '어': cup '컵', hugs '헉즈'.
1.expression: Sound excited on “Aunt Kim is coming!”, read the “Set a…” lines with a steady, even beat, ask “Is that the cat?” with a rising, surprised voice, say “Get down, Pip!” firmly, sing “Ding, dong!” brightly, and sound warm and proud on “What a big help!”

2.title: The Wrong Backpack
2.topic: a girl grabs a blue backpack after school, finds a dinosaur lunchbox inside at home, realizes it belongs to Marco, the new boy, trades backpacks with him the next morning, and they laugh and become lunch friends (school, friendship, feelings)
lines: At *home*, | she *opened* it | to get her *snack*. ↘
They *traded* *backpacks* | and *giggled* *together*. | Now they *sit* *side* by *side* at *lunch*. ↘
sounds: p·k·f 소리 뒤 -ed는 짧은 't': looked '룩트', laughed '래프트'. '룩-키드'가 아니에요!
'd'로 가볍게 붙여요: opened '오픈드', pulled '풀드'. 한 박자로 읽어요.
t·d 소리 뒤에서만 '이드'가 한 박자 더 생겨요: traded '트레이디드'.
2.expression: Read the first lines in a quick, everyday voice, gasp and sound shocked on “This isn't mine!”, let “He must have mine!” sound like an idea popping up, ask “Is this yours?” with a hopeful rising voice, make Marco's “I wondered where it went!” cheerful and relieved, and end with a happy, friendly tone.

3.title: Earthworms: Little Diggers
3.topic: earthworms: no bones, eyes or legs; a body made of rings with tiny bristles that grip the soil; stretching and squeezing to move underground; breathing through damp skin; sensing light; eating dead leaves and soil and leaving castings that feed plants; tunnels that bring air and water to roots; gently moving a sidewalk worm back to the grass (animals, science, nature)
lines: After a *rain*, | you might *see* *earthworms* | on the *sidewalk*. ↘
Earthworms have no *bones*, | no *eyes*, | and no *legs*. ↘
Their *bodies* are *made* of *rings*, | and *tiny* *bristles* | help them *grip* the *soil*. ↘
Earthworms *breathe* | through their *damp* *skin*. | That is *why* they *need* to *stay* *wet*. ↘
They *can't* *see*, | but they can *sense* *light*, | so they *hide* from the *sun*. ↘
So the *next* *time* you *see* a *worm* on the *sidewalk*, | *gently* *move* it to the *grass*. | It's a *garden* *helper*! ↘
sounds: '어'를 하면서 혀를 뒤로 말아 'r': earth '어r쓰', worm '워r엄'. '얼스'나 '웜'처럼 r을 빼지 않아요.
자음을 모음 없이 붙여요: stretch '스트레치'를 '스-트-레치'로 끊지 말고 한 번에, squeeze는 '스퀴즈'.
혀끝을 이 사이에 살짝 물어요: breathe와 their는 떨리는 소리, earth와 through는 바람 소리예요.
3.expression: Start with a curious, noticing voice on the sidewalk scene, read the “no bones, no eyes, and no legs” list with a small pause after each part, ask “How do they move?” with a clear rising voice, stretch out the word “long” and say “short” quickly to act out the movement, sound amazed on “castings, a rich food for plants,” and end kindly and proudly on “It's a garden helper!”
practice: no bones, no eyes, and no legs

4.title: Bramble Wants to Be Soft
4.topic: a young hedgehog who feels too prickly to play with the soft rabbits rolls in thistle fluff to look fluffy, but when a fox appears and the littlest rabbit freezes, he shakes off the fluff, curls into a spiky ball in front of her and the fox backs away; the rabbits welcome him, prickles and all (animals, friendship, feelings, being yourself)
lines: Every *morning*, | he *watched* the *rabbits* *tumble* in the *meadow*, | their *fur* as *soft* as *clouds*. ↘
“*Nobody* wants to *play* | with a *prickly* *ball* like *me*,” | he *sighed*. ↘
He *rolled* in a *pile* of *thistle* *fluff* | until his *spines* were *covered* in *white*. ↘
The rabbits *dashed* into their *burrow*, | but the *littlest* one, | *Clover*, | *tripped* and *froze*. ↘
Bramble *didn't* *stop* to *think*. | He *shook* off the *fluff*, | *curled* into a *tight* *ball* | and *rolled* in *front* of Clover. ↘
The fox *sniffed*, | *poked* his *nose* at the *spines*, | and *yelped*. | “*Ouch*!” ↘
From that *day* on, | the rabbits *saved* Bramble a *spot* in *every* *game*, | *prickles* and *all*. ↘
sounds: 끝의 -le는 '을'처럼 가볍게: tumble '텀블', thistle '씨슬' (가운데 t는 소리 나지 않아요).
fluff, tumble, just / fox, spot, nobody
short u는 힘을 빼고 짧은 '어': fluff '플러프'. short o는 입을 크게 '아': fox '팍스', spot '스팟'.
sighed는 '사이드', peeked는 '픽트', decided는 '디사이디드'. 앞 소리에 따라 -ed가 달라져요.
4.expression: Begin like a storyteller, slow and gentle, let Bramble's “Nobody wants to play with a prickly ball like me” sound sad and quiet, make “Now I'm fluffy, too!” hopeful and proud, drop to a tense, low voice on the dark shadow, shout “Fox!” in alarm, speed up as the rabbits dash and Bramble rolls, make the fox's “Ouch!” sharp and funny, let Clover's “Your prickles saved me!” sound amazed and grateful, and end warm and slow on “prickles and all.”
